public_rationale: The Insilico and BenevolentAI records support Marcus's description for those candidates: safety results or an exploratory subgroup signal did not establish therapeutic efficacy. However, two examples cannot establish that no qualifying drug existed. AI-assisted repurposing of baricitinib also makes the scope important: it challenges a broad reading of from AI, while falling outside the surrounding discussion of designing new drugs.
limitations: No industry-wide absence claim is inferred from individual candidates.
Company announcements are primary disclosures but are not independent efficacy assessments.
Candidate status and evidence of efficacy are not mutually exclusive.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As far as Marcus knows, AI has so far produced only candidate drugs, none yet proven to work.

statement.excerpt: but as far as I know from AI we still just have what we call candidate drugs, nothing yet proven to work.
statement.document_title: What was 60 Minutes thinking, in that interview with Geoff Hinton?

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns designing drugs, so the central reading is newly designed drugs whose molecular design materially involved AI.
Proven to work means convincing therapeutic efficacy in people, not merely laboratory activity or successful safety testing.
Regulatory approval or a successful confirmatory efficacy trial would clearly qualify; approval is not the only possible evidence of efficacy.
I treat as far as I know as an epistemic qualification, not a condition requiring access to Marcus's private knowledge.
Still and yet refer to the accumulated record through 2023-10-10.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive account of AI-designed clinical candidates shows that none had established human therapeutic efficacy by 2023-10-10.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one drug materially designed using AI had established human therapeutic efficacy by 2023-10-10.

evidence.explanation: The announcement describes these results as safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics in healthy participants, followed by entry into Phase II efficacy testing. It supports candidate status for this molecule, but cannot establish the absence of successful drugs elsewhere.

The company reported that BEN-2293 failed its overall efficacy endpoints. It also reported a subgroup signal requiring further investigation, which is weaker than established efficacy and prevents treating this as an absence of all biological activity.

The authors describe AI-assisted identification of baricitinib for COVID-19 and clinical benefit. This is material counterevidence to a broader reading covering all AI-assisted drug discovery, but the molecule was an existing treatment rather than newly designed by AI.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A candidate-level review of AI-designed drugs through 2023-10-10, linked to trial results and regulatory records, or one verified counterexample demonstrating established human efficacy within that period.
